subject: history_social
passage: In the foothills of central Nepal, Gurung honey hunters harvest the nests of the world's largest honeybee, which builds its combs high on sheer cliff faces. Twice a year, a hunter climbs a rope ladder that hangs from the clifftop, steadies himself far above the ground, and uses a long bamboo pole to cut a comb free while smoke from a fire below calms the bees. The work is dangerous and slow, yet the hunters are careful to leave part of every nest ______, so that the colony survives and the cliff can be harvested again the following season.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The hunters leave part of each nest "so that the colony survives" and the cliff "can be harvested again." For the bees to survive, part of the nest must be left unharmed, so "intact" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. An empty nest would mean the comb had been taken; the hunters deliberately leave part of it to keep the colony alive.
explanation.B: Correct. Leaving part of the nest intact, that is, whole and undamaged, lets the colony survive and rebuild for the next harvest.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The nests are already on open cliff faces; whether part of a nest can be seen has nothing to do with the colony surviving.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The nests are already exposed on "sheer cliff faces." The hunters' concern is the colony's survival, not leaving the nest open to view.
